note: CJ Stroud is playing the best football of his career this season as the QB15 in fantasy points per game. Stroud has been a QB1 in each of the last three weeks (QB5, QB13, QB5). He has six passing touchdowns across his last three games and a rushing score. Among 33 qualifying passers, Stroud is eighth in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 15th in catchable throw rate, and second in hero throw rate. Stroud should shred the Giants' pass defense. New York has allowed the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-highest EPA per dropback, and the sixth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Dak Prescott has been STRUGGLING this season as the QB17 in fantasy points per game. Over the last two games, Prescott hasn't eclipsed 14.6 fantasy points in either game. A lot of this is on Prescott, but the play designs for Dallas have been bad. Dallas was 11th in play action usage and 13th in motion rate last year. This season, Brian Schottenheimer has made everything even harder on his offense and quarterback, as Dallas has the 12th-lowest play action usage and the third-lowest motion rate. It's wild. I don't understand what Schotty is doing, but hopefully he comes to his senses soon. When you pop open the hood, Prescott hasn't been nearly as bad as I thought, and this could be correctable if Dallas gets back to their offensive bells and whistles. Among 33 qualifying quarterbacks, Prescott is 19th in yards per attempt and 17th in hero throw rate, but he is also 13th in passing success rate, first in highly accurate throw rate, and 11th in catchable target rate. Philly has still fielded a tough pass defense, allowing the sixth-lowest passing success rate, the 13th-lowest passer rating, and the 14th-lowest CPOE. Prescott should have time in the pocket, though. Philly has the fifth-lowest pressure rate and the third-lowest quick pressure rate. Prescott most likely posts low-end QB1/high-end QB2 numbers this week.

Bryce Young is balling out as the QB4 in fantasy points per game. Among 33 qualifying passers, Young is 11th in yards per attempt, 12th in hero throw rate, eighth in CPOE, and 11th in fantasy points per dropback. Young shouldn't have any issues with Tampa Bay's middle-of-the-road pass defense this week. Tampa Bay is 17th in passing touchdown rate, 19th in passing success rate, and has allowed the 11th-highest CPOE. Tampa Bay is blitzing at the fourth-highest rate, but they have the NFL's lowest pressure rate. Against the blitz, Young has been an average quarterback, ranking 12th in yards per attempt and 19th in passing success rate. Young should post QB1 numbers again this week.

After two rough outings to begin his Minnesota tenure (QB27, QB28), Kyler Murray was the QB10 in Week 5 against the Saints. Murray had two passing scores and 51 yards on the ground. That was his first game of the season with multiple passing scores and more than 17 yards on the ground. Among 33 qualifying passers, the passing numbers for Murray haven't been good, as he has the 14th-lowest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing success rate, the fifth-lowest highly accurate throw rate, and the fourth-lowest aDOT. Murray could dunk on all of this in Week 7 against a below-average Indy pass defense. Indy has allowed the eighth-most yards per attempt, the tenth-highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-highest CPOE.

Patrick Mahomes is the QB7 in fantasy points per game with at least 21.4 fantasy points in three games this season. Among 32 qualifying passers, Mahomes is fifth in yards per attempt, third in passing success rate, seventh in hero throw rate, and eighth in EPA per dropback. Mahomes can still put up QB1 numbers this week, but I'm not expecting a high-end QB1 showing. Seattle has allowed the fewest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing success rate, and the fifth-lowest passer rating.

Aaron Rodgers is the QB18 in fantasy points per game with at least 22 fantasy points in three of his last four games. He could easily be adding to the 20-plus fantasy point total this week. Among 33 qualifying passers, Rodgers has the tenth-fewest yards per attempt and the ninth-lowest passing success rate while ranking 20th in highly accurate throw rate and 26th in hero throw rate. Rodgers has flip-flopped between low aDOT point guard and Jameis Rodgers this season. Despite his weekly volatility, Rodgers could have a nice Week 7 against a struggling Saints pass defense. New Orleans has allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the fourth-highest passing success rate, and the sixth-highest CPOE.

Last week, Tyler Shough bounced back as the QB2 for the week, which was wonderful to see after two down outings and the news that he has been playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand. Overall, Shough is the QB11 in fantasy points per game. Among 33 qualifying passers, Shough is 26th in yards per attempt, 20th in passing success rate, tenth in catchable target rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. Shough should see enough passing volume to flirt with QB1 production this week, but it's not a great matchup. Pittsburgh is 19th in yards per attempt and 16th in passing success rate allowed, but they have also held passers to the seventh-fewest fantasy points per dropback and the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback. This is a below-average matchup for Shough.

Is it possible to have any confidence in plugging Bo Nix into a fantasy lineup? I'm asking for a friend...because I have none. Nix is the QB28 in fantasy points per game. Nix has only one game this season where he passed for more than 220 yards or for multiple touchdowns. It has been rough. Among 33 qualifying passers, Nix has the second-fewest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing success rate, the seventh-lowest EPA per dropback, and the second-lowest aDOT. If Nix can't succeed this week, I don't know if he will at any other time during the 2026 season. Arizona has been a wonderful matchup for nearly every quarterback this season. The Cards are allowing the most yards per attempt, the highest passing touchdown rate, and the tenth-highest passing success rate.

Deshaun Watson is the QB23 with no weekly finishes higher than QB15 since Week 2. Watson has continued to play horribly. I think it's only a matter of time for him to be benched, but the fact that the Browns are winning on the back of their defense will continue to buy him more starts. Among 33 qualifying passers, Watson is 16th in yards per attempt and passing success rate, but he has the eighth-lowest aDOT, the tenth-highest off-target rate, and the eighth-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Watson also has the third-highest pressure to sack rate with the 15th-lowest EPA per dropback. Fortunately for Watson, the Titans' secondary has been horrible, so he could post decent QB2 numbers again this week. Tennessee has allowed the 11th-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing success rate, and the second-highest CPOE. The Titans also have the eighth-lowest pressure, so Watson should see clean pockets this week.

Kirk Cousins bounced back last week with 19.5 fantasy points, which marks the fourth time he has hit or exceeded that line this season. Cousins is the QB13 in fantasy points per game. Among 32 qualifying passers, Cousins is 14th in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, 17th in highly accurate throw rate, and tenth in EPA per dropback. Cousins could post low-end QB1 numbers if the Rams come out firing as he attempts to keep pace with their offense, but he's best viewed as a solid QB2 with a tougher matchup. The Rams have limited passers to the second-fewest yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest passing success rate, and the 14th-lowest EPA per dropback.

Michael Penix is the QB21 in fantasy points per game after having a banner Week 6 as the QB5 in weekly scoring. Among 33 qualifying passers, Penix is third in yards per attempt, 11th in CPOE, 30th in highly accurate throw rate, 21st in catchable target rate, and tenth in hero throw rate. Last week was his first game of the season with more than 15 fantasy points. I don't see a standout performance in the cards for Penix for Week 7. The 49ers pass defense has been electric this season, allowing the ninth-fewest yards per attempt, the ninth-lowest passing success rate, and the 13th-lowest EPA per dropback. Penix is a low-end QB2 for this week.

Geno Smith is the QB24 in fantasy points per game, with only one game with more than 260 passing yards or multiple passing touchdowns this season (against Detroit). Smith is playing better football than all of that suggests, as he has been New York's point guard. Among 33 qualifying passers, Smith has the seventh-lowest aDOT, but he is also 12th in yards per attempt and passing success rate and first in catchable target rate. Smith could flirt with QB1 production this week against a Miami secondary that has allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the second-highest passing touchdown rate, and the highest passing success rate.

Tanner McKee limped to a QB22 finish last week. Among 29 passers, he was 26th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 16th in highly accurate throw rate, and 22nd in catchable target rate. Ok, not great. He also doesn't run, so we won't be getting production on the ground from McKee. McKee could post better numbers this week against a hapless Dallas secondary that has allowed the fourth-most yards per attempt, the third-highest passing success rate, the fifth-highest CPOE, and the highest EPA per dropback. Dallas is 14th in pressure rate, so that's a concern, but they are only 17th in quick pressure. McKee could have a nice game in Week 7.

Sam Darnold is the QB26 in fantasy points per game, but his game against Washington is still carrying all of the water there. In his two starts since that game, he hasn't had more than 14.3 fantasy points in either outing. Among 32 qualifying passers, Darnold is 17th in yards per attempt, 26th in passer rating, 23rd in passing success rate, and he has the highest turnover-worthy pass rate. Sit Darnold again this week with a tough matchup incoming. Kansas City has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per attempt, the third-lowest passing success rate, the ninth-lowest CPOE, and the second-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Jacoby Brissett has been a decent QB2 this season, as the QB21 in fantasy points per game. Among 33 qualifying passers, Brissett is 30th in yards per attempt, 14th in passing success rate, 20th in CPOE, 25th in aDOT, and 33rd in hero throw rate. Brissett is a low-end QB2 again this week with a tough matchup. Denver has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per attempt, the seventh-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 11th-lowest passing success rate.

Malik Willis has two games this season with at least 17.7 fantasy points and one QB1 finish in weekly scoring (QB12). He has rushed for at least 39 yards in three of his five games this season with two rushing scores. Among 33 qualifying passers, he has still struggled with accuracy, ranking 22nd in yards per attempt with the sixth-lowest passing success rate, the third-lowest catchable target rate, and the ninth-best hero throw rate. Willis could be a QB1 again this week against a mid-tier Jets' pass defense. New York has allowed the 12th-highest passing success rate, the 13th-highest passing touchdown rate, and the tenth-highest CPOE.

Cam Ward is the QB30 in fantasy points per game. He's not a viable fantasy option currently. Ward hasn't managed more than 10.4 fantasy points in three of his last four games. Ward hasn't thrown for more than 224 yards in any game this season, nor has he had multiple passing touchdowns in any game. We're nearing the point where Ward could get benched during a game in any week. I'm not plugging a player with this lack of production and risk profile into any fantasy lineup anytime soon.

Daniel Jones has been a disaster this season as the QB34 in fantasy points per game. There's no way that I'm starting him in any format this week. Jones has only one game this season higher than QB22 in weekly fantasy scoring. He's not running with only one game with more than ten rushing yards, and he's not making up for the lack of rushing production with his arm. Jones hasn't managed more than 270 passing yards or multiple passing touchdowns in any game. That won't change this week against Minny. Minnesota has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the lowest passing success rate, and the lowest passing touchdown rate.

Last week, JJ McCarthy came in for Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter and proceeded to almost lead the team back to a victory. In less than a quarter, McCarthy amassed 243 passing yards, one passing score, and 26 rushing yards (two rushing attempts). McCarthy finished as the QB12 in fantasy last week with ONLY ONE QUARTER OF FOOTBALL PLAYED! That's absolutely insane. Among 29 qualifying passers last week, he was first in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, and first in hero throw rate. No, I'm not expecting McCarthy to do this weekly as the new starting quarterback for the team, but it was insanely impressive. McCarthy is a solid QB2 this week who could easily post QB1 numbers. Houston is 15th in yards per attempt, 14th in passing touchdown rate, and 15th in passing success rate allowed. They also have the 12th-best pressure rate, but Houston is also 20th in quick pressure rate. McCarthy should have some clean pockets this week behind an offensive line that has allowed the 11th-lowest pressure rate.
Baker Mayfield (thumb) opened this week with a full practice. We'll see how his practice participation goes this week. I'll update his outlook on Friday, but he could be back this week.

Bucky Irving is the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.8 touches and 87.6 total yards. Irving has a 64.7% snap rate, a 59.6% rushing share, and a 47.7% route share (10.8% target share). Among 39 qualifying rushers, he is 24th in explosive run rate and 15th in missed tackle rate. Irving should post RB1/2 numbers this week with a wonderful matchup. Carolina has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 11th-highest missed tackle rate.

Braelon Allen could be the Jets' workhorse back again this week. I'll update his outlook on Friday, but Breece Hall opened this week with a DNP. Since Week 4, Allen has been the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 20 touches and 95.6 total yards. In those three games, Allen has had an 88% snap rate, 75.3% of the rushing work, and a 64% route share (10.7% target share). Among 39 qualifying rushers, Allen is 11th in explosive run rate, seventh in yards after contact per attempt, and tenth in missed tackle rate. Allen could run wild this week. Miami has allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the second-highest zone rushing success rate, the 12th-highest zone yards per carry (Allen: 59.5% zone), and the fourth-lowest stuff rate.

Chase Brown is the RB19 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19 touches and 74 total yards. In his last game before the bye, Samaje Perine did cut into his early-down workload, but I'm not concerned about Brown moving forward. In that game, Brown still had a 60.3% snap rate, a 41.9% rushing share, and a 60.6% route share (12.5%) target share. He did split the red zone rushing work with Perine, with each back seeing four red zone rushing attempts, but Brown had a 63.2% snap rate in the red zone. I think Brown's workload could bounce back this week, but even if it continues along this path, he is still the workhorse back for Cincy. Among 38 qualifying backs, Brown is 19th in yards after contact per attempt and 27th in missed tackle rate. Brown will have to get by with passing game usage and overall volume this week after laying all of that out because Baltimore's run defense has been formidable this season, allowing the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the 11th-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Woody Marks finished with 17 touches and 81 total yards with a 77.8% snap rate. He should be Houston's workhorse again this week. Marks also had a 60% route share and 8.8% target share. Marks was the RB22 for the week. Among 39 qualifying rushers, Marks is 14th in yards after contact per attempt and ninth in missed tackle rate. Marks should be a strong RB2 this week with RB1 upside. New York has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest rushing success rate, and the ninth-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Rhamondre Stevenson remained New England's lead back last week, but TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner cut into his early-down workload. Stevenson played 60.3% of the snaps with a 42.9% route share, but he had only 38.9% of the rushing work. Stevenson finished with 14 touches and 36 total yards. Overall, he has averaged 14.3 touches and 62.3 total yards this season. Among 38 qualifying rushers, Stevenson is 17th in yards after contact per attempt and 11th in missed tackle rate. Stevenson should return RB2 value this week. Chicago has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Josh Jacobs is back at practice for Green Bay. The Packers haven't committed to say that he will definitively play this week, so I'll update his outlook and the outlook of Green Bay's backfield on Friday.

In his two games as the Dolphins' starting running back, Ollie Gordon has averaged 14.5 touches and 94 total yards as the RB16 and RB14 in weekly scoring. In those games, he had a 63.4% snap rate, 51.9% of the rushing attempts, a 46.3% route share, and a 4.5% target share. He should be Miami's lead back again this week. Among 39 qualifying rushers, Gordon is fourth in explosive run rate and yards after contact per attempt. Gordon should post another nice stat line this week. The Jets' run defense has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest rushing success rate, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 2, Tony Pollard has been the RB34 in fantasy points per game, averaging 17.4 touches and 67.8 total yards. During that span, he has had two RB2 weekly finishes (RB16, RB24). Across his last five games, he has had a 56.9% snap rate, 68.4% of the rushing work, a 30.6% route share, and a 5.5% target share. Among 39 qualifying backs, Pollard has been solid, ranking 15th in yards after contact per attempt and 21st in explosive run rate. If Cam Ward can provide somewhere in the vicinity of decent quarterback play and move the offense, Pollard could be an RB2 again this week. Cleveland's run defense has been horrible, allowing the second-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

J.K. Dobbins is the RB37 in fantasy points per game with two top-24 weekly finishes this season (RB13, RB15). Dobbins has averaged 14.8 touches and 49.5 total yards. He has a 43.9% snap rate, a 55.1% rushing share, and a 16.3% route share (4.2% target share). Among 39 qualifying backs, Dobbins is 28th in explosive run rate, 23rd in yards after contact per attempt, and 35th in missed tackle rate. Dobbins could be an RB2 again this week. Arizona has allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate.

RJ Harvey has quietly been a top-24 running back in weekly scoring in three of his five games (RB24, RB12, RB13) this season. Harvey has averaged 8.8 touches and 48.8 total yards, with the bulk of his production coming in the passing game. Harvey has a 15.8% target share, 2.30 YPRR, four red zone targets, and a 10.8% first-read share. Arizona has the highest rate of two-high in the NFL (69.8%). Against two high, Harvey has had an insane 41% TPRR with 2.32 YPRR. He should see PLENTY of targets this week. Harvey is a strong flex again this week against an Arizona defense that has allowed the 11th-most yards per target to running backs.

Blake Corum has played 23-29.1% of the snaps in four of six games this season, while averaging 9.3 touches and 52.4 total yards. Corum's added passing game usage has been a nice wrinkle this season. He has at least two targets in each of his last four games, with two games with at least four targets. With Davante Adams out, I wouldn't be shocked if the Rams leaned on their strong running game even more. Over the last two weeks, Corum has been the RB13 and RB10 in weekly scoring. Among 38 qualifying backs, he is sixth in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate. Corum should have another strong week against the Raiders' run defense, which has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate while having the 13th-lowest stuff rate and sitting at 15th in missed tackle rate.

Alvin Kamara has been a limited committee back over the last two weeks, averaging seven touches and 37.5 total yards. Since Week 5, he has played only 25% of the snaps with an 18.2% rushing share and a 17.2% route share (10.9% target share). Yes, he has three scores across his last three games, but we can't count on a touchdown to save his fantasy day weekly. Kamara is a weekly sit until his role changes in the New Orleans backfield.

The Saints' backfield has dissolved into a gross three-way committee with Kendre Miller handling the bulk of the early-down work. Last week, he finished with 22 touches (20 carries) and 70 total yards. He had a 45.6% snap rate, 52.6% of the rushing work, and a 15.6% route share (6.7% target share). With the early-down volume, Miller is a viable flex option again this week. Miller's per-tough rushing efficiency has been putrid, though. He has only a 2.4% explosive run rate, 1.73 yards after contact per attempt, and a 12% missed tackle rate. If the Saints are playing from behind this week, Miller could easily get gamescripted out of the Week 7 action, so that also has to be added to his volatility. Pittsburgh hasn't been an imposing run defense, allowing the 14th-highest explosive run rate, the 11th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 14th-highest missed tackle rate. Miller needs the Saints to play with a lead this week and a touchdown to likely pay off for fantasy purposes. Both are questionable propositions in Week 7.

Roschon Johnson has been solid over the last two weeks. Over the last two games, he has had a 39.7% snap rate, a 31.6% rushing share, and a 34.1% route share (11.8% target share). He has averaged 12.5 touches and 62.5 total yards with RB31 and RB15 finishes in weekly scoring. Johnson hasn't been impressive on a per-touch basis with only 1.82 yards after contact per attempt and a 14% missed tackle rate. New England could allow him to flirt with strong flex value again this week. New England has allowed the 11th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 17th-highest missed tackle rate.

Rico Dowdle returned to the field last week. He finished with ten touches and 49 total yards. Dowdle had only a 27.6% snap rate, 31.8% of the rushing work, and a 13% route share (6.1% target share). Jaylen Warren is the clear backfield leader now. Dowdle did split the red zone work with Warren, with both backs having a 45.5% red zone snap rate and one red zone rushing attempt last week, so he does still have some touchdown equity in this offense. That and the wonderful matchup put Dowdle on the low end of the flex radar this week. New Orleans has allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

I have zero confidence in starting anyone from the Seattle backfield right now. Last week, Emanuel Wilson lost his lead back role as he played only 32.9% of the snaps while having 53.8% of the rushing attempts and only a 13.8% route share (one target). If Seattle is playing from behind in this game, Wilson could see his role eaten up by George Holani, who had a 56.1% snap rate last week. Last week, Wilson finished with 14 touches and 52 scoreless rushing yards. Among 38 qualifying backs, Wilson is 26th in explosive run rate and 25th in missed tackle rate. Kansas City has allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

I don't want to start anyone from the Giants' backfield this week. I have no clue how the coaches divide up the workload this week, even without Najee Harris. Last week, Cam Skattebo didn't have a touch, and he played only six offensive snaps. Last week, Devin Singletary, Tyrone Tracy, and Najee Harris all played at least 15.3% of the snaps and had at least 20% of the rushing work. Singletary led the group with a 39.6% route share. This backfield could be a mess this week, and the matchup is so tough I don't see any back having a great day when the volume could be capped. Houston has held rushers to the third-lowest explosive run rate while posting the tenth-highest rate of backs hit at the line of scrimmage or behind it and the fourth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Last week, TreVeyon Henderson had only a 23.5% snap share, a 19.4% rushing share, and a 20% route share (3.1% target share). Henderson finished with eight touches and 40 total yards. Corey Kiner cut into his early-down load. I expect Henderson to flirt with 8-10 touches again this week as a middling flex with a good matchup. Among 38 qualifying backs, Henderson is 28th in yards after contact per attempt and 31st in missed tackle rate. Henderson likely needs a score to pay off this week, but if he rips off a big run, he could get it. Chicago has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

In his last game before the bye, Samaje Perine finished with 16 touches, 78 total yards, and a score as Chase Brown's backfield running mate. I'm not willing to declare Perine as a standalone flex play moving forward, as that was the first game of the season where Perine had more than eight touches. In that Week 5 game, Perine played 50.8% of the snaps with 45.2% of the rushing volume, but he had only a 33.3% route share. He did split the red zone work with Brown, as each back had four red zone rushing attempts, but Brown dwarfed him in snap rate (63.2%) inside the 20-yard line. That feels like more noise than signal of Brown's role being in serious jeopardy moving forward. I'm not flexing Perine this week in a matchup that is rough on paper for early down production. Baltimore is allowing the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the 11th-lowest missed tackle rate.

Todd Monken stated that he's optimistic that Quinshon Judkins could be back this week. I'll update his outlook and the outlook for this backfield on Friday. He opened this week with a limited practice (ankle).
Breece Hall opened this week with a DNP. It could be another week before he is back in the huddle. I'll update his outlook on Friday.
David Montgomery (groin) opened with a DNP this week. I'm expecting him to be out again this week, but I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Tetairoa McMillan is having a strong season as the WR9 in fantasy points per game. McMillan, in his three games with Jalen Coker as a full-time player, has had a 22.1% target share, 2.40 YPRR, four red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 27.1% first-read share. His target share and first-read share have ranked second on the team in those games behind only Jalen Coker. In those three games, McMillan has also taken a back seat against single high to Coker. Tampa Bay has the second-highest single-high rate in the NFL (65.1%). Against single-high, in those three games with Coker, McMillan has had a 22% TPRR and 1.67 YPRR (both of these figures are behind Coker). McMillan can still have a solid week against Tampa Bay's secondary, which is 18th in yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game allowed to perimeter wide receivers, but I'm expecting Jalen Coker to lead the team in targets this week.

DeVonta Smith returned with a fury last week as the WR9. Overall, Smith is the WR10 in fantasy points per game. Last week, he had a 26.7% target share, 2.21 YPRR, one red zone target, three deep targets, and a 35.3% first-read share. Those are all alpha numbers. This week, he'll face a tougher matchup, but Smith is talented and seeing enough volume to overcome it. Dallas has held perimeter wide receivers to the sixth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest receiving fantasy points per game.

COKEHEADS UNITE! Jalen Coker is having a wonderful breakout season as the WR13 in fantasy points per game. In his three full games this season, Coker has led Carolina with a 25.7% target share and 32.9% first-read share while posting 2.95 YPRR with five red zone targets and seven deep targets. Coker should crush again this week. Tampa Bay has the second-highest single-high rate in the NFL (65.1%). Against single-high, in those three games, Coker has led the team with a 29% TPRR and 3.21 YPRR. Those are wonderful numbers. Tampa Bay is 18th in yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

George Pickens is the WR23 in fantasy points per game, drawing a 20.3% target share with 1.96 YPRR, five red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 22.4% first-read share. The matchup isn't easy this week, but if Philly continues their recent trend of single high usage, it could be a good coverage structure for his volume. Since Week 5, Philly has had the eighth-highest rate of single high (60.5%). This season, Pickens' splits against single high and two high have been dramatic. Against single high, his TPRR rises from 17% to 35%, and his YPRR jumps from 1.58 to 2.74. Philly has allowed the 13th-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers, but only one touchdown. Pickens could pile up some yardage this week, but his touchdown prospects are dimmer.

Tee Higgins is the WR20 in fantasy points per game. Higgins has a 22.8% target share with 2.63 YPRR, two red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 25.5% first-read share. Higgins is a strong WR2 again this week. Baltimore has the fifth-highest two-high rate (62.8%). Against two-high, Higgins has crushed, with his TPRR rising from 17% to 22% and his YPRR increasing from 2.15 to 3.11. Baltimore has allowed the 11th-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers.

AJ Brown returned to the huddle last week. He played his usual role as New England's clear alpha, but he had a rough day at the office with four drops. Brown finished with only three receptions and 27 receiving yards, but his usage was fantastic. Brown had a 28.1% target share (94.3% route share), three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 42.9% first-read share. This is a wonderful bounce-back spot for Brown. Chicago has the ninth-highest rate of single-high (56.1%). Against single high, Brown has had a 29% target-per-route run rate this season. Yes, he has produced only 1.0 YPRR against single high, but that is small sample variance. In 2023-2025, against single high, Brown had a 35% target-per-route run rate and 3.53 YPRR against single high. He has historically shredded single high and could do so again this week against a secondary that has allowed the most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

DK Metcalf is heating up as the WR32 in fantasy points per game with top 20 finishes in two of his last three games in weekly scoring (WR16, WR8). Metcalf has a 22.1% target share with 1.35 YPRR, three red zone targets, 12 deep targets (third most among wide receivers), and a 31.5% first-read share. Metcalf should shred the Saints secondary this week. New Orleans has the third-highest rate of single high (64.2%) in the NFL and has struggled to defend deep passing. Against single high, Metcalf's TPRR has increased from 20% to 23% while his YPRR has risen from 1.17 to 1.44. Historically Metcalf has been MUCH better against single high. Metcalf should also convert his robust downfield role into fantasy production this week against a secondary that has allowed the eighth-most deep passing yards and the highest passing success rate to downfield passing. The Saints have allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 15th in receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

Luther Burden is the WR26 in fantasy points per game after finishing as the WR13 in weekly scoring last week. Burden has a 20.7% target share with 2.31 YPRR, nine red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 26.2% first-read share. It won't be a cakewalk for Burden this week, but he could see an elevated target share with Rome Odunze likely dealing with a Christian Gonzalez shadow. Burden has the talent and a smart playcaller to overcome a tough matchup. New England has limited slot receivers to the ninth-fewest yards per target and the 11th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Over the last two games, Germie Bernard has been the WR11 in fantasy points per game. He has had a 25% target share with 2.42 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 23.1% first-read share. Bernard should keep the party bus rolling this week. New Orleans has the third-highest rate of single high (64.2%) in the NFL. Since Week 5, against single high, Bernard has had a 23% target-per-route run rate and 2.59 YPRR. The Saints have allowed the 12th-most yards per target to slot receivers while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity against the position.

Michael Wilson is the WR29 in fantasy points per game after down games over the last two weeks. Wilson has a 23.4% target share with 1.43 YPRR, nine red zone targets, nine deep targets, and a 28.9% first-read share. Patrick Surtain is back at practice on a limited basis. Patrick Surtain may play this week. If that happens, Wilson's outlook gets quite dim. I expect Surtain to return next week, but I won't rule out this week. I'll update Wilson's outlook for Week 7 on Friday once we know more about Surtain's health.

Carnell Tate is the WR42 in fantasy points per game with two top-36 weekly finishes in his last three games (WR36, WR12). Tate's problem isn't related to his play at all but to that of his quarterback. Tate has a 24.9% target share, 2.15 YPRR, two red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 33% first-read share. His weekly volatility has been directly tied to Cam Ward. We'll see if Tate can overcome a tough matchup this week and Ward's play. He's a volatile flex for Week 7. Cleveland has allowed the eighth-lowest yards per target and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Denzel Boston is the WR23 in fantasy points per game while ranking 36th in separation and tenth in route win rate among 100 qualifying receivers. Boston has an 18.4% target share with 1.82 YPRR, four red zone targets, 11 deep targets, and a 22.4% first-read share. This week, Boston has another nice coverage matchup. Tennessee has the eighth-highest two-high rate (57.9%). Against two high, Boston has seen his TPRR increase from 14% to 21% and his YPRR jump from 0.53 to 3.33. Boston is a strong flex again this week. Tennessee has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and 13th-most receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Bo Nix has crushed Jaylen Waddle's season so far as the WR49 in fantasy points per game. Waddle has a 19% target share with 1.49 YPRR, two red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 27.9% first-read share. It has been difficult to watch all season. Maybe this is the Waddle bounce-back game, but I don't know if Nix can facilitate it. Waddle has the talent to do so if Nix can just get him catchable targets. Arizona has allowed the second-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.
Emeka Egbuka popped up on the injury report this week with a DNP (concussion/foot). I'll update his outlook on Friday, but the concussion throws his availability for Week 7 into doubt.

Jameson Williams is the WR32 in fantasy points per game, despite finishing as a top-20 wide receiver in weekly fantasy scoring in each of his last two games (WR19, WR15). Williams has a 14.7% target share with 1.50 YPRR, a 31.8% air-yard share, and a 22.7% first-read share. He has three red zone targets and nine deep targets. This week's matchup doesn't line up well for Williams. Green Bay has the fourth-highest two-high rate (65.4%). Against two-high, Williams ' target-per-route run rate drops from 16% to 15%, and his YPRR has declined from 1.65 to 1.36. Not only does the coverage structure not line up for Williams, but Green Bay has held perimeter receivers to the 11th-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Well, Tre Tucker did it again. He popped off with a big game and now likely heads back into fantasy nothingness. Tucker has two games this season with at least 22.9 PRR points (22.9, 26.7). In his other four games, he hasn't hit double-digit PPR points once. In his four non-outlier games, Tucker has a 13.9% target share, 1.27 YPRR, two red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 19.3% first-read share. Tucker is a player that fantasy GMs will chase and put him in their lineups consistently and get burned more than rewarded. He is the quintessential "better in best ball" type of receiver that can cause more fantasy pain than payoff yearly. I won't be chasing this fantasy ghost. The Rams have allowed the sixth-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Devaughn Vele's star has dimmed somewhat over the last two games. Vele is the WR31 in fantasy points per game, but he has managed double-digit PPR points only once in his last four games. Vele has a 17% target share with 1.30 YPRR, five red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 21.9% first-read share. Unfortunately, I don't see Vele turning around his fantasy fortunes this week. Pittsburgh has been tough against slot receivers, allowing the fourth-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Sit Vele this week.
Last week, Omar Cooper Jr. popped off with a big game. We need to know the status of Adonai Mitchell this week before diving into Cooper's outlook for Week 7. I'll update his situation on Friday.
Rashee Rice opened the week with a DNP (hamstring). I'll update Xavier Worthy's outlook on Friday. It will vary massively depending on whether Rice is active or out.

Keenan Allen has remained a solid flex this season, despite Daniel Jones barely being a functional NFL quarterback. Allen is the WR35 in fantasy points per game with three top-36 weekly finishes (WR20, WR35, WR17). Allen has a 21.7% target share with 1.62 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 25.6% first-read share. He's a volume-based low-end flex this week only. Minnesota has allowed the 14th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

KC Concepcion is the WR74 in fantasy points per game, which is rough, but he has been playing much better than that fantasy production would have you believe. Among 100 qualifying receivers, Concepcion is 12th in separation and 38th in route win rate. He also leads the team with a 19% target share, 26.7% first-read share, and 27.3% designed target rate. Sadly, he has only produced 1.21 YPRR with three red zone targets and three deep targets. Concepcion hasn't finished as a WR3 or higher in weekly scoring this season, but this could be the week. Tennessee has allowed the second-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Malik Washington has been a volume hog as the WR37 in fantasy points per game. Washington has two top-36 weekly finishes this season (WR35, WR23). He hasn't scored a touchdown this season, but toss a touchdown on top of nearly any of his stat lines this season, and he's flirting with WR2 production for fantasy. Washington has a 27.7% target share, 1.93 YPRR, two red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 29.8% first-read share. Washington is headed for a nice game against the Jets this week. New York has the tenth-highest rate of two-high (55.9%). Against two-high, Washington has seen a 30% TPRR with 2.10 YPRR. Washington is a strong flex with WR2 upside. New York has allowed the 14th-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Josh Downs' season has quickly gone down the toilet as the WR56 in fantasy points per game. In four of his six games this season, Downs has failed to manage at least double-digit PPR points or more than 50 receiving yards. Downs has an 18.3% target share with 1.40 YPRR, five red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 23.6% first-read share. Sit Downs this week with another tough matchup incoming. Minnesota has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

I'm worried Rome Odunze will see Christian Gonzalez all day. If that's the case, I worry Odunze will have a quiet game. Odunze is the WR61 in fantasy points per game with only one outing this season with at least double-digit PPR points. Odunze has a 15.4% target share with 1.67 YPRR, four red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 17.5% first-read share. Christian Gonzalez has followed DK Metcalf, Garrett Wilson, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba this season on 65.4-86.4% of their routes. Wilson and Metcalf were held scoreless and below 50 receiving yards when lined up opposite Gonzalez. Sit Odunze this week, if possible.

Wan'Dale Robinson is the WR36 in fantasy points per game with two top-36 weekly finishes in his last three games (WR19, WR28). Touchdowns and cheap PPR value have helped to keep Robinson's fantasy value afloat. In his last three games, he has scored twice while snagging at least six receptions twice. Robinson has a 20.3% target share with 1.29 YPRR (6.03 aDOT), five red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 26.1% first-read share. Robinson offers sneaky flex value again this week with a good matchup. The Browns have allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Last week, DeMario Douglas had a 58.8% snap rate, a 74.3% route share, a 25% target share, 86 receiving yards (3.31 YPRR), and a 19% first-read share. It was the third time this season that Douglas has had a route share north of 70%, but he also has two games where his route share dipped below 60%. His usage has been up and down over the last two seasons, which makes me skeptical that it will hold in Week 7. Overall, Douglas has a 65.2% route share, a 14.8% target share, 1.62 YPRR, three red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 16.9% first-read share. Chicago has the ninth-highest rate of single-high (56.1%). Against single-high, Douglas has a 23% TPRR, but his YPRR has fallen from 1.85 to 1.40. Douglas is flex-viable this week, but there's a ton of volatility with his projection. Chicago has allowed the 14th-fewest yards per target and the 15th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers. It's essentially a neutral matchup for Douglas.

In the two games Jordan Addison has played this season with Kyler Murray, he has had a 21.2% target share with 1.89 YPRR, zero red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 34.2% first-read share. It has to be mentioned that Justin Jefferson didn't play in those two games, so take those numbers with a grain of salt. In Weeks 1-2, with Addison and Jefferson on the field together, Addison had only a 15.9% target share with 0.47 YPRR, one red zone target, zero deep targets, and a 16.7% first-read share. The reality of his usage and production on a weekly basis is probably somewhere in the middle of those two polarities, but Addison is only a low-end flex with a bad matchup this week. Indy has limited perimeter wide receivers to the third-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity.

With Tank Dell also in the mix this week, I have no clue what Jaylin Noel's playing time will be this week. Whenever Noel is on the field, he is producing, but Nick Caley and the coaching staff refuse to play him in a full-time role. Over the last two games, Noel has been the WR36 and WR16 in weekly scoring. Over the last two games, Noel has had a 48.4% snap rate, a 54.9% route share, a 23% TPRR, a 13.2% target share, 3.79 YPRR, and a 13% first-read share. With Noel's usage up in the air for Week 7 and a tough matchup incoming, I'm sitting him in most leagues. New York has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Last week, Dontayvion Wicks disappeared from the passing offense, with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert both leading the way. Wicks had only an 8.9% target share and 8.8% first-read share, as his route share fell to 60.4%. Sit Wicks this week. We have to see how many weapons Tanner McKee can support before believing in a tertiary receiver like Wicks.

Chris Godwin is an easy sit this week. Godwin still hasn't posted a week with at least double-digit PPR points or a top-36 finish in weekly scoring. Godwin has a 14.9% target share with 1.10 YPRR and a 16.5% first-read share. Carolina has limited slot receivers to the third-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Add Courtland Sutton to the list of skilled players sunk by Bo Nix's putrid quarterbacking. Sutton hasn't had even double-digit PPR points in any game this season. Sutton has a 13.8% target share with 0.78 YPRR, six red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 21.2% first-read share. I'd love to tell you to play Sutton this week because the matchup is wonderful, but I don't have any faith that Nix will turn the Titanic around this week. If you're desperate, Sutton is a flex play this week because of the matchup only. Arizona has allowed the second-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Kendrick Bourne has had some flex value this season with two outings with at least 12 PPR points. Bourne has an 11.9% target share with 1.34 YPRR, five red zone targets, one deep target, and a 14.5% first-read share. Bourne is flex viable again this week. I'm not expecting a massive game, but he can give you some PPR production in a pinch. Denver is 17th in yards per target allowed to slot receivers while giving up the 14th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Ja'Kobi Lane remains more of a speculative rest-of-the-season add for fantasy purposes than a player anyone should be looking to flex for Week 7. Last week, Lane had only a 55.3% route share with a 16.1% target share and 22.7% first-read share. His usage was encouraging, but the route share is still concerning. I can't start a part-time player this week against a secondary that has limited perimeter receivers to the fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity.

Last week, Marvin Harrison Jr. had a 25.7% route share, an 11.8% target share, and a 17.4% first-read share in his first game with Houston. We have to see how quickly Harrison Jr.'s role grows with Houston before plugging him into a fantasy lineup. Their wide receiver room was already messy, but Tank Dell will also be back this week. Sit Harrison Jr. again this week.

Makai Lemon is someone who could pop off with a randomly strong game this week. So far this season, Lemon hasn't scored a touchdown and hasn't had more than 43 receiving yards in any game. That could change this week. Last week, Lemon had an 89.6% route share with an 11.1% target share, 6.20 aDOT, 19 receiving yards (0.44 YPRR), and a 14.7% first-read share. Is any of that outside of his route share good? Nope. Dallas has been having ISSUES with stopping slot receivers, though. Dallas has allowed the most yards per target, the most receiving yards, and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers this season. Lemon is an intriguing flex this week.

Efton Chism is an interesting deep-league dart throw this week. Over the last two games, Chism has had snap shares of 80.3% and 61.8% with route shares of 65.8% and 25.7%. His target share in these two games has also been all over the map with 17.6% and 3.1%. What gives me hope for Chism is his usage against single-high this season. Chicago has the ninth-highest rate of single-high (56.1%). Against single-high, Chism leads the team with a 32% TPRR and 2.42 YPRR. With the Pats always deploying matchup-specific game plans weekly, it wouldn't shock me at all if Chism is heavily utilized this week. If that's the case, Chism could have a strong performance. Chicago has allowed the most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

In Weeks 3-5, Chris Bell had a 13.8% target share (68.8% route share), 1.02 YPRR, four deep targets, and a 14.8% first-read share. The matchup for Bell this week against the Jets isn't in his favor. He's a sit this week. New York has the tenth-highest rate of two-high (55.9%). Against two-high, Bell has only an 8% TPRR and 0.18 YPRR. I don't see him improving upon those numbers this week. The Jets have limited perimeter wide receivers to the fourth-fewest yards per target and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.
Caleb Douglas only managed to participate in limited drills to open this week. I'll update his outlook on Friday, but I think he's probably another week away from returning.

Isaac TeSlaa has been a forgotten fantasy hype piece outside of his WR26 finish in weekly scoring in Week 4. I'm not going out on a limb and starting TeSlaa in most formats, but he's on the deep league desperation flex radar this week. Green Bay has the fourth-highest two-high rate (65.4%). Against two-high, he has seen his target-per-route run rate jump from 7% to 16% and his YPRR climb from 0.45 to 2.29. He also has some touchdown equity in the Detroit offense with three end zone targets this season. Green Bay has been stingy to perimeter wide receivers, so tread carefully, but if he provides flex value this week, I won't be surprised. Green Bay has held perimeter receivers to the 11th-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.
Rashee Rice opened with a DNP (hamstring) this week. I'll update his outlook on Friday.
Adonai Mitchell doesn't have an oven mitt on his hand anymore. He opened this week with a limited practice (finger). We'll see if he makes it back this week, but I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Colston Loveland has started to resemble the player that we thought he'd be for 2026 over the last three weeks. Yes, during this stretch he has only been the TE14 in fantasy points per game, but in those three games his usage has trended upward. Since Week 4, Loveland has had a 19.1% target share (70.2% route share) with 1.62 YPRR, six red zone targets, and a 26.2% first-read share. Loveland could be a TE1 again this week with targets being pushed in his direction, with Rome Odunze facing a Christian Gonzalez shadow. New England is 17th in yards per target while allowing the fifth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. New England held Dalton Kincaid, Pat Freiermuth, and Brenton Strange to quiet days, but Brock Bowers destroyed them with eight grabs, 110 receiving yards, and a score. I don't project a blow-up game for Loveland, but he could still be a low-end TE1 this week.

Travis Kelce is still motoring along as the TE7 in fantasy points per game. Among 38 qualifying tight ends, Kelce is 13th in target share (16.5%), third in YPRR (2.41), fourth in FD/RR (0.121), and tenth in first-read share (19.1%). Kelce has three red zone targets and two deep targets this season. Kelce won't have it easy this week, but he could still post a TE1 week as he presents an easier outlet for Mahomes than attacking Seattle's talented corners. Seattle has allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Dallas Goedert was the TE14 for the week with a 17.8% target share, 61 receiving yards (1.65 YPRR), and a 23.5% first-read share. Those are all solid if not damn good numbers. Goedert should be competing for the second spot in the target pecking order this week for Philly. He could easily be a TE1 this week. Dallas has allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Juwan Johnson is the TE9 in fantasy points per game, but he, too, has fallen on hard times over the last two games with 5.6 and zero PPR points. Johnson has a 13.6% target share with 1.43 YPRR, seven red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.9% first-read share. This week, Johnson should return to the friendly confines of TE1 land against a defense that has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Harold Fannin is the TE13 in fantasy points per game, with two TE1 finishes this season in weekly scoring (TE3, TE12). Fannin has a 16.7% target share with 0.97 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 14.7% first-read share. This week's matchup is more favorable for KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston and tougher for Fannin. How many weapons can Deshaun Watson support weekly? Usually one, and maybe some weeks two, so this week I'm inclined to stream a tight end over starting Fannin. Tennessee has allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Kyle Pitts' usage has trended up over the last two games as the TE7 and TE2 in weekly scoring. Since Week 5, Pitts has had a 67.1% route share, a 71.1% snap rate, a 19.1% target share, 1.92 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 20% first-read share. All of those metrics are outstanding. Unfortunately, I don't think Pitts keeps the train rolling this week. The 49ers have the tenth-highest rate of single high (55.7%). Since Week 5, against single high, Pitts has had only a 10% TPRR and 0.25 YPRR. The 49ers have also held tight ends to the seventh-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Sit Pitts this week, but better days are ahead for him.

T.J. Hockenson was concussed in Week 5, but I'm hoping/expecting him to be back this week. In Weeks 1-4, Hockenson had two TE1 weekly finishes (TE9, TE1) while seeing five red zone looks and scoring a touchdown. During that four-game span, Hockenson had a 22.7% target share, 2.14 YPRR, and a 23.5% first-read share. Some of those numbers are pumped up by Justin Jefferson's absence. Hockenson could still be a TE1 this week with Jefferson in the huddle. Indy is 15th in receiving fantasy points per game against tight ends while giving up the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

If there was ever a matchup for Mark Andrews to break out of his fantasy funk, it's this one. Andrews is the TE25 in fantasy points per game, despite having a 19.6% target share and 21.7% first-read share. He has only had one touchdown despite seeing five red zone targets and one deep target. Andrews has an encouraging 0.091 FD/RR, but his YPRR has fallen to 1.37. If Andrews can't post a TE1 week in Week 7, then it's probably getting close to cut bait time for fantasy rosters. Cincy has allowed the most yards per target and the eighth-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends.

Hunter Henry is the TE18 in fantasy points per game, with TE1 finishes in weekly scoring in each of the last two games (TE8, TE6). Henry has a 12.2% target share, 1.63 YPRR, five red zone targets, one deep target, and a 13.6% first-read share. Henry is on the streaming radar this week against a defense that has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends this season.
Dalton Schultz sustained a quad injury last week. He opened this week with a DNP. I'll update his outlook on Friday.

With Brock Bowers in the lineup, Michael Mayer is the TE10 in fantasy points per game with at least 12.2 PPR points in three of those four games. Since Week 3, Mayer has had a 13.6% target share with 1.90 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and an 11.1% first-read share. Temper your expectations this week, though. The Rams have allowed the fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends this season.

AJ Barner hasn't managed double-digit PPR points in any game this season, but he is on the streaming radar this week. Barner has an 11.6% target share with 0.87 YPRR, five red zone targets, and an 11.9% first-read share. The Chiefs have been a shutdown unit against wide receivers, but they have allowed the third-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Carolina split the tight end duties between Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller. Last week, Waller had only a 45.9% snap rate, a 42.9% route share, a 5.1% target share, and 7.7% first-read share. He didn't secure either one of his two targets. Waller is a risky deep-league streamer only. Tampa Bay has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity.

Jake Ferguson's fantasy value has tanked this season as the TE25 in fantasy points per game. Ferguson has only a 9.8% target share, 0.69 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and an 8.4% first-read share. The matchup isn't good enough for Ferguson to sniff the random streamer radar. Philly is 15th in yards per target allowed to tight ends, but they are also holding the position to the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity (only two receiving scores). Sit Ferguson.

Well, my deep dive on Darnell Washington went well last week, as Washington was the TE9 in fantasy scoring and could have finished even higher if he had secured a target in the end zone and hauled in a second touchdown. This week, we're going back to the Washington well. Last week, Washington had a 71.1% snap rate, a 50% route share, a 10.2% target share (19% TPRR), 25 receiving yards (0.93 YPRR), and a 9.4% first-read share. I dove deep last week into Washington and Pat Freiermuth's splits against single and two high, so I won't rehash all of that this week with both tight ends. Freiermuth isn't in this week's Primer because his usage against single high has been non-existent over the last two seasons. The Saints have the third-highest rate of single high (64.2%). Against single high this season, Washington has a 24% TPRR and 1.86 YPRR. Both are strong numbers. New Orleans has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Washington is back on the streaming radar this week.

Ok, I know you're surprised to see Evan Engram's name here, but the matchup is fantastic for him this week if Bo Nix can play even close to the level of a league-average quarterback. Engram popped off as the TE8 in fantasy in Week 1, so we know his upside as a streaming option is in there somewhere. Engram has a 9% target share with 1.20 YPRR, two red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 10.6% first-read share. No, none of those numbers are good. That's why he is a desperation or deep-league streaming option only. Arizona has the highest rate of two-high in the NFL (69.8%). Against two-high, Engram is second on the team with a 23% TPRR while logging 1.89 YPRR. Arizona has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since his return in Week 5, Mason Taylor has had a 58.8% route share with a 15% target share, 1.43 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 12.5% first-read share. During the same two-game stretch, Kenyon Sadiq has had only a 29.4% route share and 10% target share. Taylor has been the Jets' starting tight end over the last two games. He's on the streaming radar this week against a hapless Miami secondary. Miami has allowed the second-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Carolina split the tight end duties between Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller. Tremble had only a 47.6% route share with a 10.3% target share and 11.5% first-read share. He secured all four of his targets for 46 receiving yards and two scores (two red zone targets). Tremble is a risky deep league streamer only. Tampa Bay has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity.
